title: fix(inbox): sanitize unpaired UTF-16 surrogates in DM bubbles
body:
## Summary

- Adds `StringUtils.sanitizeUtf16` — strips unpaired UTF-16 surrogate code units, returns the same instance when input is already well-formed
- Applies it once at the top of `MessageBubble.build` so substring/split and the downstream `Text` widget all see clean input
- New unit tests for the sanitizer and a widget test asserting `MessageBubble` doesn't crash on an unpaired surrogate

## Why

NIP-17 rumor bodies and other sender-controlled text reach the app via JSON `\uXXXX` escapes that can carry unpaired surrogates. Strict UTF-8 in the local nip44 path catches byte-level malformations, but JSON-decoded escape sequences slip through. Flutter's text renderer asserts well-formed UTF-16 and crashes with `Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16`, taking out the open conversation. Surfaced in production logs after PR #4451 made the inbox usable on staging.

Closes #4463.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/utils/string_utils_test.dart` — 8 sanitizer cases (ASCII identity, empty identity, emoji preserved, unpaired high/low/trailing dropped, valid pairs around unpaired)
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/inbox/conversation/widgets/message_bubble_test.dart` — 29 cases incl. new surrogate-doesn't-crash assertion

title: Notifications: refresh auth, support stable cursors, and speed comment targets
body:
## Problem
The notifications flow has multiple regressions around Funnelcake integration and notification target routing:

- NIP-98 auth events can be reused beyond Funnelcake's 60-second freshness window, causing notification pagination requests to fail when a cached token ages out.
- Funnelcake notification pagination now returns stable cursor pairs, but the mobile client does not consistently parse `next_cursor_id` or send `before_id` on follow-up requests.
- Tapping comment and reply notifications waits on target resolution work before navigating, which makes the interaction feel slow even when the destination can already be inferred.
- Notification target resolution should prefer uppercase `A` root addressable tags when present so comment notifications resolve to stable NIP-33 video routes instead of older event IDs.
- Explicit cursor overrides must win over stored cursor state so pagination does not accidentally reuse a stale `before_id`.

## Goal
Make notification pagination and deep linking reliable again by refreshing auth in time, supporting stable cursor pagination semantics, and reducing perceived latency when opening comment-related notifications.

## Scope
- Refresh or reissue NIP-98 auth before Funnelcake rejects a request for token age.
- Parse and persist stable notification cursor pairs, including `next_cursor_id`.
- Send `before_id` on subsequent notification page requests when the server provides a stable cursor pair.
- Navigate into comment and reply targets immediately, then complete target loading inside the opened screen.
- Prefer uppercase `A` root addressable tags in the notification resolver when present.
- Preserve explicit cursor override behavior so overrides do not silently fall back to stored pagination state.
- Remove any now-blocking analyzer noise directly related to the touched code path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Notification pagination continues working when previously cached auth would have exceeded Funnelcake's 60-second freshness requirement.
- Follow-up notification page requests send the correct stable cursor fields expected by Funnelcake.
- Comment and reply notification taps show the destination route immediately instead of waiting for resolver work to finish first.
- Notifications that include an uppercase `A` root addressable tag resolve to the stable video route derived from that tag.
- Passing an explicit cursor override does not reuse a stored `before_id` from prior pagination state.
- Regression coverage exists for auth freshness, notification cursor parsing, repository pagination behavior, resolver routing, and notification tap navigation.

## Context
- Related backend work: divinevideo/divine-funnelcake#400
- This work is focused on reliability and responsiveness in the mobile notifications experience.

title: Inbox: 'Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16' renders DM/notification text
body:
## Symptoms

While the Inbox tab is open, the app logs Flutter framework errors:

```
[SYSTEM] Flutter Error: Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16
Flutter framework error: Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16
```

Observed 3 times in a single session on staging while the inbox was visible (logs at 17:14:52, 17:15:04, 17:15:23).

## Timing evidence (points at DM, not notifications)

Each occurrence is immediately preceded by a batch of `nip44_decrypt` RPC calls:

```
[Keycast RPC] nip44_decrypt completed in 378ms (HTTP 200)
[Keycast RPC] Calling nip44_decrypt...
[Keycast RPC] nip44_decrypt completed in 394ms (HTTP 200)
[17:15:04.609] [SYSTEM] Flutter Error: Invalid argument(s): string is not well-formed UTF-16
```

The notification REST path (`/api/users/:pk/notifications`) is plain JSON — no nip44 involved. The clustering with `nip44_decrypt` strongly suggests this fires from **DM conversation rendering** (decrypted message previews / message bubbles), not the notification list.

## Likely root cause

A Dart `String` is being constructed from decrypted bytes (likely via `utf8.decode(..., allowMalformed: true)` somewhere in the nip44 decrypt path), which can produce strings containing **unpaired UTF-16 surrogates**. Flutter's text engine then throws when it tries to render them.

## Candidate code paths to investigate

- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/widgets/message_bubble.dart` — message text rendering
- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view.dart`
- The keycast nip44 decrypt boundary — wherever decrypted bytes become a Dart `String`. Check whether bytes are decoded with `allowMalformed: true` and not subsequently sanitized.

## Suggested fix shape

At the decrypt → String boundary, sanitize unpaired surrogates, e.g.:

```dart
String sanitizeUtf16(String input) =>
    String.fromCharCodes(input.runes); // drops unpaired surrogates
```

This is a band-aid at the rendering boundary — the better fix is to ensure the decrypt path never produces a malformed string in the first place (treat bytes as UTF-8 strictly, log + skip the message if it fails).

## Reproduction

Open the Inbox tab on staging with a logged-in user that has at least one DM conversation. The errors fire shortly after the inbox loads and decrypts message previews.

## Not the cause (already ruled out)

- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/notification_actor_spans.dart` uses `indexOf` + `substring` on the same string. Those cuts are always on UTF-16 code-unit boundaries by construction, so they can't split a surrogate pair unless the input already contains an unpaired surrogate — i.e. this widget is at most a victim, not a source.

## Surfaced by

Diagnostic logging added in #4451 (notification fetch error context), which made the inbox-load failure path visible in the same session.

title: fix(push): send push control events to Divine relay with relay OK handling
body:
## Summary

Push registration could look successful even when the Divine relay never accepted the event.
This change sends push registration, deregistration, and preference events directly to the configured Divine relay and waits for a relay OK response.
It also keeps the publish bounded so a late relay connection cannot write or queue a stale push-control event after the timeout.

## What Changed

Push control events now use the same targeted OK-confirmed publish path.
The relay layer now treats the caller timeout as one deadline for both sending and waiting for OK responses.
Same-URL fallback now distinguishes a failed send from a sent frame, and deadline-bound sends cannot queue stale EVENT messages.

- Route kinds 3079, 3080, and 3083 through `publishEventAwaitOk` with `targetRelays: [EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl]`.
- Let explicit target-relay OK publishes run even when the general relay pool has no connected relays.
- Skip the generic disconnected-relay retry when explicit target relays are provided.
- Bound `RelayPool.sendEventAwaitOk` with one deadline across `_sendCollect` plus OK waiting.
- Thread that deadline through `Relay.send`, `RelayBase.send`, and `WebSocketConnectionManager.sendJson`.
- Disable pending-message queueing for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Do not queue pending-auth messages for deadline-bound await-OK sends.
- Remove expired temp relays after deadline timeout so their connection waiters cannot flush stale control events.
- Track expected relays as soon as each send succeeds, so timeouts report the relays that actually received the frame.
- Avoid retrying a stalled same-URL normal target as a temp relay after the shared deadline is consumed.
- Allow same-URL temp fallback when the normal target path returns `false` immediately without sending.
- Log accepted, rejected, and no-response relay outcomes without logging encrypted push-control content.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4411

## Testing

I tested the push-control service paths, the client OK-publish wrapper, and the relay-pool timeout and fallback behavior.
I also verified the touched packages and the app analyzer after the SDK API change.

- `dart format packages/nostr_client/lib/src/nostr_client.dart packages/nostr_client/test/src/nostr_client_test.dart packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay_pool.dart packages/nostr_sdk/test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib/relay/relay.dart lib/relay/relay_base.dart lib/relay/relay_isolate.dart lib/relay/web_socket_connection_manager.dart lib/relay/relay_pool.dart test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart test/unit/relay_pool_auth_test.dart test/unit/relay_count_test.dart test/integration/relay_auth_test.dart test/integration/nip50_search_test.dart`
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/src/follow_repository_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/src/nostr_client_test.dart --plain-name "publishEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart --plain-name "sendEventAwaitOk"`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/unit/relay_pool_concurrency_test.dart`
- `dart test test/unit/publish_outcome_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/services/push_notification_service_test.dart`
- `flutter test --no-pub test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart`
- `dart analyze` in `mobile/packages/nostr_sdk`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/nostr_client`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile/packages/follow_repository`
- `flutter analyze --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `flutter test --no-pub` in `mobile`
- `git diff --check`

## Risks

The main behavior change is that explicit target publishes no longer wait for unrelated pool reconnects, and deadline-bound OK publishes no longer queue messages for later delivery.
That is intentional for push control events because a late queued control event can make the app report a failed publish while still mutating relay-side push state later.
The SDK `Relay.send` interface now accepts an optional deadline, so custom test relays and package-local fake relays were updated to match.

- A target URL already present in the normal relay pool is not retried as a temp relay after the normal path sends or queues the frame.
- A normal target path that returns `false` immediately can still fall back to a same-URL temp relay within the caller timeout.
- If the normal target path stalls until the shared deadline is exhausted, the publish fails fast instead of trying the same URL a second way.
- If a relay connects after the deadline, the deadline-aware send path returns false before writing the stale EVENT.
- This does not prove the push service processed the event after relay acceptance; it only confirms relay acceptance.

title: fix(push): send push control events to Divine relay with relay OK handling
body:
## Summary
Mobile push control events need to reliably reach the Divine relay path consumed by `divine-push-service` so real FCM push registration, deregistration, and preference updates work in production.

## Context
Recent investigation found:

- PR #4162 fixes the signer-readiness race by delaying registration until a signer-backed Nostr session is ready.
- A prod-emulator test showed generic relay-pool publishing could report success while the kind `3079` event landed on a user relay (`nos.lol`) instead of `relay.divine.video`.
- A targeted diagnostic run against `wss://relay.divine.video` showed the relay rejected `3079` with `blocked: kind 3079 not in allowed list`.
- Relay-side allowlist/discovery work is tracked in `divine-funnelcake#380`.
- First-party mobile does not publish kind `1` events today.
- Mobile consumes kind `1` for mention-style notifications.
- Mobile comments/replies are currently published as kind `1111`.
- This issue should not expand mobile push preferences to `1111` or `30023`.

## Scope
- Publish push control events directly to `EnvironmentConfig.relayUrl`.
- Await NIP-20 relay `OK` for push control events.
- Use a bounded `5s` relay OK timeout.
- Log relay outcomes:
  - `acceptedBy`
  - `rejectedBy`
  - `noResponseFrom`
- Apply targeted relay + OK behavior to:
  - `3079` push registration.
  - `3080` push deregistration.
  - `3083` push preferences.
- Preserve the readiness-driven registration lifecycle from PR #4162.
- Preserve token-refresh re-registration behavior, but make refreshed-token registration use the same targeted relay + OK path.
- Keep `p` tags targeting `EnvironmentConfig.pushServicePubkey`.
- Keep existing `NotificationPreferences` trigger kind list unchanged for now: `[1, 3, 7, 16]`.
- Add temporary relay-layer diagnostics for push control kinds `3079/3080/3083` during rollout.
- Keep permanent push-control logs in `PushNotificationService`.
- Do not add a durable retry/background scheduler in this issue.

## Current Mobile Kind Contract Notes
- `1`: consumed for mention-style notifications; not first-party published by mobile; not current comments/replies.
- `3`: follows/contact-list.
- `7`: likes/reactions.
- `16`: generic reposts.
- `1111`: current mobile comments/replies, but not yet advertised in `3083` preferences.
- `30023`: mobile can consume long-form mentions locally, but not yet advertised in `3083` preferences.

## Out of Scope
- Adding `1111` to mobile push preferences.
- Adding `30023` to mobile push preferences.
- Changing canonical notification trigger-kind policy.
- Adding relay-side allowlist changes.
- Adding durable retry queues or background retry scheduling.

title: Notifications: prefer human-readable actors in grouped rows
body:
## Problem
Grouped notification rows can surface the wrong lead actor when the newest actor does not have a useful human-readable display name.

Current behavior can show:
- a hash-like actor name instead of a recognizable display name
- `Unknown user` as the lead actor even when another grouped actor has a valid explicit name

That makes grouped notification rows harder to scan and lowers confidence in who actually triggered the notification.

## Goal
Prefer a human-readable actor name for grouped notification rows so the most visible actor label is informative and consistent with the existing generated display-name fallback behavior.

## Scope
- Choose an explicitly named actor as the lead actor when grouped notification data includes one.
- Fall back to the existing generated display-name behavior when the newest actor name is hash-like or otherwise not suitable for display.
- Preserve the current grouped notification behavior outside actor-name selection.
- Add regression coverage for grouped notifications where the newest actor has a hash-like name and another actor has a better explicit display name.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Grouped notification rows prefer an actor with a useful explicit display name over a newer actor whose display name is hash-like.
- `Unknown user` is not shown as the lead actor when a valid named actor is available in the grouped row.
- Existing display-name fallback behavior remains intact for actors without usable names.
- Regression tests cover grouped notification ordering and actor-name selection for the hash-like-name case.

## Context
This work is focused on improving notification readability without changing the underlying notification grouping model.

title: fix(notifications): retry transient 5xx + offline-cache fallback for inbox refresh
body:
## Description

Hardens the in-app notifications inbox against transient failures of `relay.divine.video/api/users/<hex>/notifications`. Today a single `500` from that endpoint wipes the inbox UX because:

1. `FunnelcakeApiClient.getNotifications` has no retry on `5xx`/timeout.
2. `NotificationRepository` re-throws on the first failure.
3. `NotificationsDao` is dead cache — `upsertNotification` exists but the repository never writes through, so nothing can hydrate the inbox on cold start.
4. `NotificationFeedBloc` collapses every failure into a Retry-only screen even when WS-delivered items already sit in the snapshot.

The mobile changes here close (3) and (4) and add a bounded retry layer to soften (1)/(2). The underlying server 500 is owned by `divine-relay` and is being tracked separately.

### What changed

- **Repository (`NotificationRepository`)**
  - Bounded retry on first-page fetch — 3 attempts, full-jitter backoff capped at ~1.5 s — only for `5xx`, `408`, `429`, and `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`. `4xx` (auth / validation) still surfaces immediately.
  - Write-through to `NotificationsDao.replaceAll` on every successful first-page emission so a future cold start can render cached rows before the network responds.
  - Cold-start hydration: constructor kicks off a best-effort load from the DAO and emits placeholder rows on the snapshot (replaced as soon as the first REST/WS arrival lands).
  - New `lastRefreshError` field on `NotificationPage` — set on terminal failure of a first-page fetch, cleared on the next successful one.

- **DAO (`NotificationsDao`)**
  - New `replaceAll(List<NotificationCacheRow>)` performs a transactional delete + bulk insert. `NotificationCacheRow` is a plain Dart record so callers don't need to depend on `package:drift`.

- **BLoC (`NotificationFeedBloc` / `NotificationFeedState`)**
  - New `refreshError` boolean on state — mirrors `page.lastRefreshError`.
  - `failure` status now only fires when the cache is also empty. Cache + refresh failure → `loaded` + `refreshError: true`, so the cached items stay visible.

- **View (`NotificationsView`)**
  - New private `_RefreshErrorBanner` renders inline above the list when `refreshError && notifications.isNotEmpty`.
  - The existing `_FailureBody` (Retry-only screen) is reserved for true empty-cache hard failure.
  - All copy via `context.l10n` (`notificationsRefreshError`, `notificationsRefreshErrorRetry`).

### Reproduction

1. Sign in.
2. Block `relay.divine.video/api/users/<pubkey>/notifications` at the network layer (Charles Proxy, DNS, or wait for the server to throw `500`).
3. Open the inbox cold.

**Before:** full-screen failure with only a Retry button; cached/WS-delivered items dropped.

**After:** cached rows render with an inline 'couldn't refresh — showing what you have' banner and a Retry chip. Network recovers → banner clears on the next successful refresh.

User-report logs that surfaced this:

```
[ERROR] [SYSTEM] (RelayNotificationApiService) Notifications API error: 500
URL: https://relay.divine.video/api/users/<hex>/notifications?limit=50&before=<now>
Response: {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

**Related Issue:** Closes #4438. Refs epic #4200, user reports #4418, #4430, #4436.

## Out of Scope

- Server-side fix for `relay.divine.video` 500s — tracked separately in `divine-relay`.
- Push-control event reliability — already in flight as #4411 / #4417.
- Notification row visual changes — #4412.
- Unifying unread state across surfaces — already shipped #4247.

## Verification

- `cd mobile && dart format <changed files>` — clean.
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — `No issues found`.
- `flutter test packages/notification_repository` — `All tests passed!` (89 tests, includes new retry / write-through / hydration / clear-on-success coverage).
- `flutter test packages/db_client/test/src/database/daos/notifications_dao_test.dart` — `All tests passed!` (27 tests, includes new `replaceAll` cases).
- `flutter test test/notifications` — `All tests passed!` (124 tests, includes new empty-cache vs cached-with-error BLoC paths).
- Manual smoke plan (for reviewers): debug build with `relay.divine.video` blocked at network layer → inbox shows cached items + banner; unblock → banner clears on next refresh.

User reports could publish invalid NIP-56 `e` tags when there was no related event.
That happened because the local synthetic target `user_<pubkey>` was also being sent as an event tag.
This change keeps that synthetic target for local report history, but only sends real 64-character hex event ids as NIP-56 `e` tags.

title: Fix user reports emitting invalid NIP-56 e tags
body:
## Problem

Mobile user-report events can emit invalid NIP-56 report targets.

`ContentReportingService.reportUser()` falls back to a synthetic event id when no related event is provided:

```dart
final eventId = (relatedEventIds != null && relatedEventIds.isNotEmpty)
    ? relatedEventIds.first
    : 'user_$userPubkey';
```

That value is then used as the NIP-56 `e` tag in `_createReportingEvent()`:

```dart
['e', eventId, nip56Type],
['p', authorPubkey, nip56Type],
```

For DM user reports, `ConversationActionsCubit.reportUser()` calls `reportUser()` without `relatedEventIds`, producing kind `1984` events like:

```text
e tag: user_<64-char-pubkey>
p tag: <64-char-pubkey>
```

This is not a valid event id. Funnelcake currently aggregates report events through `report_counts_mv`, which expects `e` tag targets to be 64-char event ids. In production, ClickHouse has stored kind `1984` report events with invalid `e` targets matching this mobile format, for example:

```text
user_e680e1c186eb8d618dbd5db1e18ec4b84fdd79fddb3987692f640a33a09cf3db
```

Those malformed report events can cause Funnelcake insert failures when `report_counts_mv` tries to write the target into `FixedString(64)`.

## Scope

Update mobile user-report event construction so user reports do not place `user_<pubkey>` in a NIP-56 `e` tag.

Suggested behavior:

- For user reports with no related event id, use the `p` tag as the target and omit the `e` tag.
- For user reports with one or more real related event ids, include valid `e` tags only for actual 64-char event ids.
- Preserve the `p` tag with the reported user's pubkey and the NIP-56 report type.
- Preserve existing local report history and user-facing report flow behavior.

## Relevant Code

- `mobile/lib/services/content_reporting_service.dart`
- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation_actions/conversation_actions_cubit.dart`
- Related dialog path: `mobile/lib/widgets/report_content_dialog.dart`

## Test Plan

- Add or update unit tests for `ContentReportingService.reportUser()` with no `relatedEventIds`.
- Assert the produced kind `1984` event does not contain an `e` tag with `user_<pubkey>`.
- Assert the produced event includes a `p` tag for the reported user pubkey with the report type.
- Add/update tests for `reportUser()` with valid related event ids and assert only valid event ids are emitted as `e` tags.
- Add/update tests for DM conversation user reporting to cover the no-related-event path.
- Manually verify reporting a DM user still succeeds from the UI.

## Dependency / Coordination Notes

Funnelcake should also defensively filter `report_counts_mv` to ignore malformed `e` targets, because relays should not rely on all clients being well-formed. This mobile issue fixes the known client-side producer of `user_<pubkey>` `e` tags.

title: fix(notifications): retry transient 5xx and hydrate inbox from cache when relay API fails
body:
## Parent

Epic #4200 — execution order step 1 (unread/data correctness) and adjacent debt cleanup.

## Summary

Three independent user reports (one Android in #4430, two iOS in #4418 + #4436) show the same cold-open failure: `relay.divine.video/api/users/<hex>/notifications?limit=50&before=<now>` returns HTTP 500, the client immediately rethrows, the BLoC emits `failure`, and the user sees a Retry-only blackout despite (in two of the three cases) the bottom-nav badge already showing a non-zero unread count from a separate path.

## Reproduction

1. Sign in on iOS or Android.
2. Block (or wait for the server to fail) `relay.divine.video/api/users/<pubkey>/notifications`.
3. Open the inbox.

Expected: cached notifications render with an inline 'couldn't refresh' affordance.
Actual today: full-screen failure with only a Retry button; cached state is dropped on the floor.

User logs include the line:

```
[ERROR] [SYSTEM] (RelayNotificationApiService) Notifications API error: 500
```

## Root cause (mobile client)

- `FunnelcakeApiClient.getNotifications` has a 15 s timeout but no retry on transient `5xx` / timeout.
- `NotificationRepository.getNotifications` re-throws on the first failure, so a brief server hiccup wipes the inbox.
- `NotificationsDao` is a dead cache today — `upsertNotification` exists but the repository never writes through. Existing cached rows can't help on cold start.
- `NotificationFeedBloc` collapses every failure (network, transient, terminal) into a single `failure` status, so the view shows a Retry-only screen even when the repository's `BehaviorSubject` already held WS-delivered items.

The server-side `500` itself is a `divine-relay` problem and is being tracked separately; this issue is purely the mobile resilience gap.

## Scope (mobile-only)

- Add bounded retry + full-jitter backoff in `NotificationRepository` for the first-page fetch — only for `5xx`, `408`, `429`, and request timeouts. `4xx` still surfaces immediately.
- Write through to `NotificationsDao` on every successful first-page emission.
- Hydrate from `NotificationsDao` on construction so the inbox renders cached rows before the network responds.
- Surface a `lastRefreshError` signal on `NotificationPage` → mirrored as `state.refreshError` on `NotificationFeedBloc`.
- Inline 'couldn't refresh' banner in `NotificationsView` when `refreshError && notifications.isNotEmpty`. Full `_FailureBody` only fires on true empty-cache hard failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First-page transient `5xx`/timeout failures retry up to 3 attempts with jittered backoff before surfacing.
- [ ] `4xx` (auth, validation) surfaces immediately without retry.
- [ ] Successful first-page refreshes persist to `NotificationsDao`.
- [ ] Cold start hydrates the snapshot from `NotificationsDao` before REST resolves.
- [ ] When the cache is non-empty and the refresh fails, the view shows cached items + an inline banner — not the Retry-only failure screen.
- [ ] Empty cache + failed refresh still shows the existing `_FailureBody` with Retry.
- [ ] `notificationsRefreshError` / `notificationsRefreshErrorRetry` keys land in `app_en.arb`.
- [ ] Repo, BLoC, DAO, and view tests cover retry, write-through, hydration, banner, and full-failure paths.

## Non-goals

- Server-side fix for `relay.divine.video` 500s (tracked separately).
- Push-control event reliability (#4411 / #4417).
- Notification row visual changes (#4412).
- Unifying unread state across surfaces (already shipped via #4247).

## Engineering standard (per #4200)

- No new technical debt; clears adjacent debt (dead `NotificationsDao` cache wired in).
- One PR targeting `main`. No stacking on #4411/#4412.
- Uses existing typed exceptions from #4271 (`FunnelcakeApiException`, `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`).

title: fix(android): default useLegacySurface to true to close FlutterJNI renderer race (#3416)
body:
## Description

Closes #3416. Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` (regressed on 1.0.13 build 502 — Samsung SM-S918W).

```
java.lang.RuntimeException: Cannot execute operation because FlutterJNI is not attached to native.
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.ensureAttachedToNative
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer.scheduleEngineFrame
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage
  at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer$PerImageReader.lambda$new$0
  at android.media.ImageReader$1.run
```

### Root cause

PR #3762 narrowed the race between `ExoPlayer`'s decoder pipeline and `TextureRegistry.SurfaceProducer.ImageReader` callback dispatch — but explicitly acknowledged a residual 1–2 frame window (`stop()` and `clearVideoSurface()` are async; in-flight `MediaCodec` output can still land in a detaching `ImageReader`, and the `onImage` callback then invokes `FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame()` after `FlutterJNI` is detached). On Samsung SM-S918W's fast decoder, that residual fires.

Five callsites in the app use `useTexture: true` and **inherit the default** `useLegacySurface: false`, opting them — accidentally — into the SurfaceProducer/ImageReader path:

- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_editor/main_editor/video_editor_canvas.dart:443`
- `mobile/lib/screens/video_metadata/video_metadata_preview_screen.dart:82`
- `mobile/lib/screens/video_metadata/video_metadata_cover_screen.dart:72`
- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_clip/video_clip_preview.dart:61`
- `mobile/lib/widgets/video_metadata/modes/classic/video_metadata_classic_preview_thumbnail.dart:81`

`infinite_video_feed.dart:654–657` explicitly sets `useLegacySurface: true` and is the only callsite that's safe today. The original `SurfaceProducer` motivation (PR #3856) was the feed's Vivo/Android-16 compat, but PR #3242 migrated the feed to `infinite_video_feed` (legacy surface) — so nothing in the repo currently needs `SurfaceProducer` for its intended purpose; it's in use only via the unsafe default.

### Fix

Flip the default of `useLegacySurface` from `false` to `true` at every layer — Dart controller, MethodChannel fallback, and Kotlin function signature — so the three defaults agree and no future direct caller can trip over an asymmetry. All five accidentally-vulnerable callsites inherit the safe default and stop hitting the race in one change. SurfaceProducer remains available via explicit `useLegacySurface: false` for callsites that genuinely need OEM surface-recreate callbacks — there are none today.

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `divine_video_player_controller.dart:51` | `useLegacySurface = true` (was `false`) |
| `divine_video_player_controller.dart:27–46` | Docstring rewritten to document the new default and the explicit opt-in for SurfaceProducer trade-off |
| `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin.kt:135` | MethodChannel fallback flipped to `true` so direct callers without a Dart shim also land on the safe default |
| `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt:207` | Kotlin function default `useLegacySurface = true` (was `false`) — aligned with the Dart controller and the MethodChannel fallback |
| `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt:62–75, 180–202` | Field-level comment and `enableTextureOutput` KDoc rewritten to mark `SurfaceTextureEntry` as default and `SurfaceProducer` as the explicit opt-in |
| `DivineVideoPlayerInstanceTest.kt` | Existing SurfaceProducer tests opt in via `useLegacySurface = false` explicitly; added two new tests pinning the legacy-branch contract (`createSurfaceTexture()` called, `createSurfaceProducer()` not called; eager surface attach on materialized players) |

The 5 vulnerable callsites are intentionally **not** edited — they now inherit the safe default automatically. This keeps the diff minimal and documents that the fix is at the API layer, not the callsite layer.

### Why this is a complete fix for #3416

- The crash signature is fundamentally a race between Flutter SDK's internal `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage` (inside `FlutterRenderer`, outside our code) and `FlutterJNI` detach.
- The race cannot be closed from inside the SurfaceProducer disposal path without invasive `MediaCodec.flush()` reflection (rejected as overkill by PR #3762).
- It **can** be closed by ensuring no app callsite uses the SurfaceProducer/ImageReader path. After this fix, no `lib/` callsite does — and the safe choice is now the default, so future code is protected too.
- PR #3762's three-layer disposal hardening (Instance.dispose, Plugin.onDetachedFromActivity, PlatformView.dispose) is preserved unchanged — it remains the contract for any explicit `useLegacySurface: false` opt-in.

## Reproduction (pre-fix)

1. Real Android device (the crash signature is most reliably reproduced on devices with fast MediaCodec output queues — Samsung SM-S918W per Crashlytics).
2. Open the app. Navigate: **video editor → video metadata (preview / cover) → pooled video feed**.
3. Repeat the breadcrumb 10–20× per session.
4. Background the app while a video is playing on one of the editor / metadata screens.
5. Force-finish the activity from recents, or close the app.
6. Repeat across several launches.

Pre-fix: Crashlytics records the `FlutterJNI is not attached to native` exception under issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a`. Volume is low (1.0.13: 1 user / 1 fatal in May 15 sample) because the race window is small, but it is **fatal** when it fires.

Post-fix: the editor / metadata / clip-preview screens render via the legacy `SurfaceTextureEntry` backend, which has no `ImageReader` and therefore cannot fire the offending callback after engine teardown.

## Out of Scope

- **`media_kit_video` Android backend hardening.** If the pooled-video-feed fallback (only reached when `InfiniteVideoFeed.isSupported` is `false`, which is not Android in production) has a parallel race family, it needs its own PR scoped to the third-party media_kit. Tracked separately when needed.
- **iOS sibling #4400** (FVP / FVPFrameUpdater / ProVideoEditorPlugin / VideoTextureOutput post-teardown callbacks).
- **Reflection-based `MediaCodec.flush()` synchronous fence.** PR #3762 rejected as overkill; not needed once this change takes the volume to zero.
- **Manually editing each of the 5 vulnerable callsites.** Default-flip is strictly cleaner — it covers future code too.

## Verification

Local:

- [x] `dart format` on changed Dart file — no churn
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` from `mobile/` — no issues
- [x] `flutter analyze` from `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test` from `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` — **154/154 pass**
- [x] `flutter test` from `mobile/packages/infinite_video_feed` — **150/150 pass**
- [x] `./gradlew :divine_video_player:testDebugUnitTest` from `mobile/android/` — **17/17 pass** (15 existing SurfaceProducer / disposal contract tests + 2 new legacy-branch tests)
- [x] Comprehensive callsite audit (`grep -rEn "useTexture\s*:\s*true"` across `mobile/`) — confirmed 5 vulnerable callsites all inherit the new default; only `infinite_video_feed` explicitly sets `useLegacySurface: true`; no callsite explicitly sets it to `false`.

Manual (requires real Android device — not run from this PR; recommended before / immediately after merge):

- [ ] Repeat the reproduction breadcrumb above 20× per build on a real Android device. Expected: no crash, no black-frame regression on the 5 affected screens.
- [ ] Post-release: watch Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` for ≥1 release. Expected: events drop to zero.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Risk Register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vivo/Android 16 compositor event on the 5 affected screens causes black surface (no surface-recreate callback) | Low — those flows are short-lived and not permission-dialog-heavy | Recoverable (user navigates back/forward) | Strictly better than a fatal crash; if a Crashlytics black-frame signal emerges on those screens, the callsite can explicitly pass `useLegacySurface: false` with a documented justification |
| Hidden external consumer relying on the old default | None — workspace package, no external consumers | — | — |
| Existing tests pin the old default | None — Dart tests don't assert the default; existing Android `SurfaceProducer` tests now opt in explicitly via `useLegacySurface = false`; new legacy-branch tests pin the production path | — | All 154 + 150 + 17 (Android Kotlin) tests green |

Exception:

```text
java.lang.RuntimeException: Cannot execute operation because FlutterJNI is not attached to native.
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.ensureAttachedToNative (FlutterJNI.java:515)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame (FlutterJNI.java:1013)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer.scheduleEngineFrame (FlutterRenderer.java:1324)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage (FlutterRenderer.java:633)
at FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer$PerImageReader.lambda$new$0 (FlutterRenderer.java:517)
at android.media.ImageReader$1.run (ImageReader.java:951)
```

## Start here

This is not the already-filed back navigation issue by itself. Existing issue #2796/PR #2795 guarded app MethodChannel back navigation after engine detach. This crash is in Flutter renderer / `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer`, probably tied to Android platform views or texture-backed video surfaces still producing frames after engine detach/surface disposal.

Likely code areas:

- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerViewFactory.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_widget.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player` lifecycle if pooled feed uses platform/texture rendering on Android.
- `mobile/android/app/src/main/kotlin/co/openvine/app/MainActivity.kt` only if engine/activity lifecycle ordering is involved.

Relevant local context:

- `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.dispose()` removes callbacks/listeners and releases `textureEntry`.
- Android platform views use `PlatformViewLink` / `AndroidViewSurface` in `divine_video_player_widget.dart`.
- `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin` pauses players on lifecycle pause/resume but only disposes all on engine detach.

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. Do not assume the previous FlutterJNI back-button fix covers this.

- Reproduce or instrument Android lifecycle while video editor/metadata and pooled feed surfaces are active.
- Trace whether `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer` corresponds to `Texture` usage, Android hybrid composition, or Flutter engine internals triggered by our video widgets.
- Verify disposal order: Flutter widget removed -> platform view disposed -> ExoPlayer surface cleared -> texture released -> engine detached.
- Confirm whether any `Surface`, `SurfaceTextureEntry`, `PlayerView`, or ExoPlayer instance can emit frame callbacks after the Flutter engine is detached.
- Compare event variants in Crashlytics if needed; there are multiple variants under this same issue.

## Suggested fix direction

Possible areas to validate:

- Ensure every Android video surface clears the player and releases the surface before engine/activity detach.
- Add lifecycle-aware stop/dispose guards for video players on `onDetachedFromActivity`, not only `onDetachedFromEngine`.
- Avoid retaining `PlayerView` / `Surface` references beyond view disposal.
- If using texture output, explicitly detach the video surface and stop rendering before `textureEntry.release()`.

## Verification

- Add Android unit tests where practical around plugin/view dispose ordering.
- Run `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` tests and relevant Android tests.
- Manually test rapid navigation: video editor -> metadata -> pooled feed -> background/foreground -> close app.
- After release, confirm Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` stops receiving events.
